content.user_title: Write Better Code with Test-First Development
content.value_statement: Feature work and bug fixes can ship with weak tests when testing comes after implementation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through strict test-first cycles, failure verification, minimal implementation, and refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Guides red-green-refactor work for features, bug fixes, refactoring, and behavior changes.
Requires a failing test before production code changes.
Provides good and bad test examples using TypeScript.
Includes verification checklists for failing and passing test runs.
References mock and test utility anti-pattern guidance.
Defines stop conditions when tests are written after code.
limitations: Does not provide runnable automation or scripts.
Requires project-specific test commands from the user or repository.
Can be too strict for prototypes or generated code without human approval.
Focuses on testing discipline, not framework-specific setup.

use_cases.title: Implement a Feature Test First
use_cases.description: Guide a developer from a single failing behavior test to minimal implementation and safe refactoring.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression with Proof
use_cases.description: Turn a reported bug into a failing regression test before applying the smallest reliable fix.

use_cases.title: Improve Mock-Heavy Tests
use_cases.description: Review tests that assert on mocks and redirect them toward real behavior and simpler dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner feature or small bug fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me implement this change with TDD. First identify the smallest failing test, then wait for the failure result before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Regression Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this bug into a regression test. Describe the expected failure, ask me to run it, then guide the minimal fix.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor After Green
prompt_templates.prompt: My focused tests now pass. Help me refactor without changing behavior, and keep the verification steps explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Test Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of mocks and test design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this test plan for TDD discipline. Flag tests written after code, mock assertions, missing failure proof, and weak verification steps.

output_examples.input: Add retry support to an operation helper.
output: Starts by naming one observable retry behavior.
Asks you to run the focused test and confirm the expected failure.
Limits implementation to the passing behavior before refactoring.
Creates a regression test that rejects an empty email.
Requires proof that the test fails for the missing validation.
Guides the smallest validation change and then verifies green tests.

output_examples.input: Review tests that use many mocks.
output: Identifies assertions that only prove a mock exists.
Suggests testing real behavior or mocking at a lower boundary.
Checks whether each mock matches the real dependency contract.

best_practices: Watch each new test fail for the expected reason before implementation.
Add the smallest production change that makes the current test pass.
Refactor only after focused and related tests are green.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation first and adding tests after.
Asserting that mocks exist instead of verifying real behavior.
Expanding scope during the green phase without a failing test.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent to ask for and use project-specific test commands.

faq.question: Can I use it for bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for a failing regression test before the fix.

faq.question: Does it support refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports refactoring only after tests are green and behavior is protected.

faq.question: What frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It is framework-neutral. The examples use TypeScript, but the workflow applies across languages.

faq.question: How does it treat mocks?
faq.answer: It discourages testing mock behavior and recommends real behavior tests when practical.

faq.question: When should I not use it?
faq.answer: Ask for human approval before skipping TDD for prototypes, generated code, or configuration-only changes.
